title: 2026 Minimal Change Disease (微小病變腎病) 分子機轉、病理特徵、次發性原因與 KDIGO 指引實戰
stem: A 5-year-old child presents with periorbital edema and anasarca following a viral upper respiratory infection. Urinalysis reveals 4+ proteinuria, negative blood, and no casts. The patient is presumed to have Minimal Change Disease and is started on high-dose oral prednisone therapy. However, 8 weeks later, the patient remains heavily nephrotic without any reduction in proteinuria. A kidney biopsy is performed. Which of the following is the most important histopathologic evaluation to prevent the misdiagnosis of Minimal Change Disease in this steroid-resistant patient?

options.text: Staining for circulating anti-PLA2R antibodies by indirect immunofluorescence
Adequate sampling of the juxtamedullary glomeruli to exclude Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis
Electron microscopy for the identification of subendothelial electron-dense deposits
Assessment of C3 dominant deposition in the mesangium to rule out C3 Glomerulopathy

stem: A 32-year-old male with recently diagnosed Minimal Change Disease presents with left flank pain, macroscopic hematuria, and a sudden rise in serum creatinine from 0.9 mg/dL to 2.1 mg/dL. He has been taking high-dose prednisone for the past 2 weeks but remains heavily nephrotic (serum albumin 1.6 g/dL, 24-hour urine protein 12 g/day). An urgent Doppler ultrasound of the kidneys is performed. Which of the following mechanisms is the primary driver of this patient's acute vascular complication?

options.text: Steroid-induced hypercoagulability and endothelial activation in the renal microvasculature
Hypovolemia-induced severe reduction in renal plasma flow causing ischemic tubular necrosis
Urinary loss of Antithrombin III and hepatic overproduction of clotting factors leading to Renal Vein Thrombosis
Autoantibody-mediated activation of the complement cascade causing thrombotic microangiopathy

title: 2026 Minimal Change Disease (微小病變腎病) 分子機轉、病理特徵、次發性原因與 KDIGO 指引實戰
stem: A 25-year-old female with steroid-dependent Minimal Change Disease is planning to become pregnant. She has been in remission for 6 months on a maintenance regimen of Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF) 1 g twice daily. She is currently 6 weeks pregnant. What is the most appropriate management regarding her immunosuppressive therapy?

options.text: Continue Mycophenolate Mofetil at the current dose throughout pregnancy to prevent relapse
Switch Mycophenolate Mofetil to Cyclophosphamide to maintain remission
Discontinue Mycophenolate Mofetil immediately and initiate a Calcineurin Inhibitor (e.g., Tacrolimus) or Azathioprine
Taper Mycophenolate Mofetil over 3 months and initiate lifelong Rituximab infusions

stem: Which of the following cellular or molecular events is considered the primary initiating mechanism in the pathogenesis of idiopathic Minimal Change Disease?

options.text: Deposition of circulating immune complexes in the subepithelial space
Direct cytopathic viral infection of glomerular endothelial cells
T-lymphocyte dysfunction leading to the production of a circulating podocyte permeability factor
Genetic mutation in the COL4A5 gene causing defective type IV collagen synthesis
